choices.term: τῆς θείας δόξης καταπλουτήσαντες τὴν περιστολήν
choices.english: enriched with the covering of divine glory
choices.why: περιστολή is a covering or garment, the image used throughout.

choices.english: the righteous alone will be changed
choices.why: Only the righteous are changed; all are raised incorruptible.
Read as the perfect passive of κατέχω, as with κάτοχον ('held fast by corruption') in Cyril's comment on 1 Corinthians 15:35.

choices.term: ὁ μετασχηματισμὸς οὐκ εἰς ἑτέραν τινὰ φύσιν
choices.english: will not carry us off into some other nature
choices.why: Negation kept: we remain human, but incorruptible and glorified.

pass_a_gloss: [The opening words, 'of the image of his Son', finish Romans 8:29 and are given in the previous section.] For admittedly the bodies of all will live again clothed (καταμφιέννυμι) with the grace of incorruption, but not all will be changed (ἀλλάσσω); but the base (φαῦλος) will remain behind (ἀπομένω) in the shape (σχῆμα) of dishonour upon the one need alone of being punished (κολάζω), while the righteous alone (μόνοι) will be changed, in addition to the good of incorruption, and having been enriched with the covering (περιστολή) of the divine glory. He himself, accordingly, by his own power and a God-befitting working, 'will transform the body of our lowliness (ταπείνωσις), conformed (σύμμορφος) to the body of his glory.' And what sort is the body of our lowliness? This one from earth, the one held fast (κατέχω) by death from that ancient curse (ἀρά), which Christ has loosed (λύω), 'having become a curse on our behalf.' And the transformation (μετασχηματισμός) will be not carrying us away into some other nature, for we shall be what we are, that is men, but incomparably better; for incorruptible and indestructible (ἀνώλεθρος), and besides this glorified. And what the last trumpet that raises up (διανίστημι) the dead would wish to make plain, the divine Paul himself will make clear (σαφηνίζω) to us, saying, 'That the Lord himself in a command (κέλευσμα), in a voice of an archangel' [the quotation continues in the next section].
pass_b_english: For admittedly the bodies of all will come back to life clothed with the grace of incorruption, but not all will be changed (1 Corinthians 15:51). The wicked will remain in the form of dishonor, only so that they may be punished; but the righteous alone will be changed, and, besides the good of incorruption, they will be enriched with the covering of divine glory.

So He Himself, by His own power and a working fitting for God, “will transform the body of our lowliness to be conformed to the body of His glory” (Philippians 3:21). And what is the body of our lowliness? This body from the earth, held fast by death because of that ancient curse (Genesis 3:17–19), which Christ undid by “becoming a curse for us” (Galatians 3:13).
The transformation will not carry us off into some other nature. For we shall be what we are, that is, human beings, but incomparably better: incorruptible and imperishable, and glorified besides.

What the last trumpet that raises the dead is meant to show (1 Corinthians 15:52), the inspired Paul himself will make clear to us when he says (1 Thessalonians 4:16), “For the Lord Himself, with a cry of command, with the voice of an archangel…
